newsitem.title: CANADA: Newbridge shares surge further after AGM.
newsitem.headline: Newbridge shares surge further after AGM.

text.p: Shares in Newbridge Networks Corp continued to bask in investor favor on Friday after upbeat meetings for analysts and shareholders in Ottawa on Thursday and the announcement of a long-awaited Japanese deal.

One trader said a number of positive reports spilled out of U.S. investment houses on Friday after Thursday's analysts' gathering and the annual meeting. One analyst who had a hold on the stock upgraded his rating to a buy.
"You had a very good reception to the (analysts') meeting yesterday," said Robert MacLellan, an analyst at Dillon Read.
"You have got the Matsushita agreement. That was fundamentally built into the stock at around US$74. It isn't at US$61," MacLellan added.
Newbridge said on Thursday signed a supply deal with Japan's Matsushita Communication Industrial Co.
The company said that the deal, anticipated for months by industry analysts, was its largest ever in Japan and would add to revenues.
"It represents significant upside potential for Newbridge's revenue," president Peter Sommerer told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
The length of the supply deal and its estimated worth were not disclosed because of confidentiality agreements with Matsushita, said Newbridge spokesman Paul Goyette.
MacLellan estimated the value of the agreement could be up to C$250 million over five years.
The stock was trading 2-3/8 higher at 63-1/2 in New York and added 3.20 to 87.10 in Toronto.
"(The Matsushita) announcement at the AGM on Thursday took everybody by surprise. It had been on the rumor mill for so long that people kind of forgot about that," MacLellan said.
Cowen and Co analyst Jim Kedersha said the firm maintained a strong buy on Newbridge.
"We continue to be very bullish. The feedback we are getting from customers is very positive," Kedersha said.
Vojtek Uzdelevicz, another Cowen analyst, said: "One thing that is really important here -- they really understand the need to rebuild credibility."
Newbridge has enjoyed renewed market favor since some disappointing quarters last year sent it into a tailspin and analysts issued warnings ahead of the company's fiscal first-quarter release.

Analyst Nikos Theodosopoulos at UBS Securities in July cut the stock to a hold from a buy, raising concerns about the quarter. But when the numbers were released in August, Newbridge delivered an upside surprise, beating even the high-end street estimates.
Theodosopoulos on Friday reversed his rating change, upping his rating on Newbridge to a buy from a hold.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
